evals.name: routes-a-lint-rule-away-from-the-file
evals.prompt: Copilot keeps writing default exports in our React components. Add a rule so it stops.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is enforceable by an ESLint rule (import/no-default-export), recommends the lint rule over an instruction line, and only writes a path-scoped instruction if the user insists or lint cannot cover it. Does not silently add a line to copilot-instructions.md.

evals.name: generates-a-matched-scoped-pair
evals.prompt: We use both Claude Code and Copilot. I want a rule that anything under src/api/ must return our shared error envelope from src/api/errors.ts. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: Detects the existing layout first, then writes both .claude/rules/<topic>.md with paths: and .github/instructions/<topic>.instructions.md with applyTo:, notes in each that the pair exists, and states the verification commands (/context and /instructions).

evals.name: declines-scan-and-generate
evals.prompt: Scan this repo and generate a good CLAUDE.md for it.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back with the reason (LLM-generated context files measurably underperform; init fossilization), offers the audit path and an interview-driven alternative instead. Does not just run /init-style generation.

evals.name: diagnoses-an-ignored-rule
evals.prompt: I put 'always run migrations before starting the server' in CLAUDE.md and Claude ignores it about half the time. Why?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that must-happen-every-time rules belong in a hook rather than advisory context, mentions within-session compliance decay, and tells the user to confirm the file actually loaded with /context before assuming the rule is at fault.
